deposits.notes:
Authors' repository, also listed as both data_url and code_url in the screening form. Unauthenticated project page, node metadata, OSF Storage listing, all seven folder listings, and children endpoint returned HTTP 200. Node metadata explicitly says public=true; no child nodes. The recursively enumerated inventory is complete: 28 CSVs, seven R Markdown analysis scripts and 12 Qualtrics survey files. All 28 CSVs and seven R Markdown files were downloaded and read in memory (each below 20 MB). No explicit license is set in OSF node metadata, and no license file appears in the complete inventory.

Study mapping: Exp1=S1; Exp2A=S2; Exp2B=S3; Exp3=S4; Exp4=S5; Exp5=S6. Participant exports have unique ResponseId values and actual Condition fields. Observed arm values are Chatbot/Control in Exp1, Chatbot/Google/None in Exp2A, ChatbotHuman/HumanOnly in Exp2B, and Chatbot/Google in Exp3-5. The second randomized factors are NumCon in Exp4 and Empathy in Exp5. Main CSVs contain original idea fields. Separate rating.link CSVs hold ResponseId, workerId, idea_text and idea_text_id; the scripts explain the idea-index joins and aggregation to participant scores. The empty first column in the link CSVs is an exported row index, read as X by R and used as the idea identifier in some experiments.

Lay-rating CSVs contain numeric 1-7 responses in columns such as 1_creative_1 through 1_creative_3 and 1_practical_1 through 1_practical_3; Exp5 uses condition-specific names such as 1_creative_H_1. Expert files contain idea_id and Novelty, Practicality, Articulate and Verbosity columns with ha/ya/ak rater suffixes where measured. Exp4 and Exp5 expert files contain Novelty and Practicality only. Exp2B additionally has notnew/incnew/radnew columns for each of the three experts. Numeric score values, not just column names, were confirmed. All seven link CSVs have nonempty idea_text on every row.

rows_checked=1118 refers specifically to the raw Exp1.main.qualtrics.csv, excluding its header. columns_checked is a selected union of actual headers across the inspected files, not a single merged table. All listed CSV row counts exclude the header; no extra Qualtrics question-label/import-ID rows were present. Raw rows, output rows and judge rows must not be mistaken for analyzed participant counts. File-by-file inspection: Exp1/Exp1.rating.link.csv: 400 rows, 5 columns; Exp1/Exp1.main.qualtrics.csv: 1118 rows, 66 columns; Exp1/Exp1.main.qualtrics.handcoded.csv: 263 rows, 94 columns; Exp3/Exp3.main.qualtrics.csv: 575 rows, 108 columns; Exp3/Exp3.rating.qualtrics.csv: 217 rows, 2204 columns; Exp4/Exp4.rating.link.csv: 405 rows, 5 columns; Exp4/Exp4.main.qualtrics.csv: 547 rows, 70 columns; Exp1/Exp1.rating.qualtrics.csv: 513 rows, 2437 columns; Exp2A/Exp2A.rating.link.csv: 291 rows, 5 columns; Exp2A/Exp2A.rating.qualtrics.csv: 316 rows, 1786 columns; Exp2A/Exp2A.main.qualtrics.csv: 428 rows, 70 columns; Exp2B/Exp2B.main.ChatbotOnly.csv: 100 rows, 4 columns; Exp2B/Exp2B.rating.link.csv: 300 rows, 5 columns; Exp2B/Exp2B.rating.qualtrics.csv: 349 rows, 1852 columns; Exp2B/Exp2B.main.qualtrics.csv: 356 rows, 76 columns; Exp3/Exp3.rating.link.csv: 197 rows, 5 columns; Exp4/Exp4.rating.qualtrics.csv: 396 rows, 2470 columns; Exp5/Exp5.rating.link_Baseline.csv: 197 rows, 5 columns; Exp5/Exp5.rating.link_EmpathyHigh.csv: 194 rows, 5 columns; Exp5/Exp5.rating.qualtrics.csv: 388 rows, 2387 columns; Exp5/Exp5.main.qualtrics.csv: 575 rows, 75 columns; Robustness_Experts/Exp4.rating.experts.csv: 405 rows, 7 columns; Robustness_Experts/Exp1.rating.experts.csv: 400 rows, 13 columns; Robustness_Experts/Exp2A.rating.experts.csv: 291 rows, 13 columns; Robustness_Experts/Exp2B.rating.experts.csv: 300 rows, 22 columns; Robustness_Experts/Exp3.rating.experts.csv: 197 rows, 13 columns; Robustness_Experts/Exp5.rating.experts_Baseline.csv: 197 rows, 7 columns; Robustness_Experts/Exp5.rating.experts_High.csv: 194 rows, 7 columns.

Direct ResponseId checks linked all 400 Exp1 idea rows to 236 raw participant records with Condition; all 197 Exp3 link rows, all 405 Exp4 link rows, and all 197 baseline plus 194 high-empathy Exp5 link rows matched main-export records with Condition. Exp2B has 300 idea-link records: 200 match human participant records with Condition and 100 correspond to the separate ChatbotOnly output file; the script constructs synthetic IDs for those AI-only outputs. They must not be counted as people. Exp2A.main.qualtrics.csv was successfully read with HTTP 200 (428 raw rows and its Condition/ResponseId/idea columns), but a later optional re-download returned HTTP 403 at the OSF file service; no attempt was made to bypass it. Its link file has 291 distinct ResponseId records and nonempty texts. A cross-file match count for Exp2A was not obtained in the later check.

Reanalysis requires applying the authors' completion, demographic, attention-check, nonsensical-response and missing-rating filters before computing analyzed counts and arm statistics. Generated cleaned/joined CSV intermediates referenced by scripts are not separate files in this inventory; they can be reconstructed from the posted inputs. deposits.notes: The paper's supplementary-material DOI resolved to https://www.nature.com/articles/s41562-024-01953-1 with HTTP 200. A direct request to that publisher URL also returned HTTP 200. Both responses were the same 3,038-byte script/challenge shell with /_fs-ch-* assets and no supplementary-file links, rather than the article or a file listing. Stopped without executing the challenge, logging in, or attempting a bypass. The paper names Supplementary Notes A-K, but their files and contents could not be independently inventoried through this landing page. The local source PDF contains the main article and Reporting Summary, not those supplementary notes.

Independent reproduction deposit, DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/NK6EV, found by both DataCite title/author searches and the OSF title search. The project, node metadata, OSF Storage listing and children endpoint all returned HTTP 200 without login; public=true, no children, and four top-level files. OSF has node_license=null and no explicit license file was found. This is a secondary copy/reanalysis, not an additional randomized study.

Codes_results_data.zip (1,951,275 bytes; HTTP 200) was opened in memory. It contains five DOCX reports/code documents plus two Excel workbooks. Codes_Coitaetal.zip (1,668,497 bytes; HTTP 200) was also opened and contains the same five named DOCX documents but no data workbook. The two standalone PDF reports were inventoried from the API; their contents were not needed to classify the workbooks.

Codes_results_data/My_Exp1_cleaned.xlsx, sheet 'Sheet 1': 233 rows, with ResponseId, Condition, idea, idea_text_raw, idea_count_jc, ORIGINALITY, APPROPRIATENESS, OVERALL and the six component scores. Condition counts read from this table are Chatbot=103 and Control=130. ResponseId, Condition, idea, idea_text_raw and all three composite-score columns are nonmissing on all 233 rows. rows_checked and columns_checked refer to this workbook.

Codes_results_data/My_Exp3.analysis.dataset.xlsx, sheet 'Sheet1': 194 rows, with ResponseId, Condition, System, ORIGINALITY, APPROPRIATENESS, OVERALL, DELIVERY, exposition_aid, other process measures and component scores. Condition counts read from this table are Chatbot=95 and Google=99. ResponseId, Condition and the three creativity composite-score columns are nonmissing on all 194 rows. This workbook does not contain idea/idea_text/idea_text_raw; S4 diversity needs the authors' OSF source texts. has_texts_or_ideas=true here is supported by S1 only. The reports discuss more experiments, but the confirmed participant data in this deposit cover only S1 and S4.

Both workbooks were inspected with pandas from in-memory BytesIO objects. These are reproduction-provided analyzed tables; their row counts and arm counts were observed directly, not inferred from the article. Their complete equivalence to an independently rerun original analysis was not audited.

Complete inventory: seven Jupyter notebooks and requirements.txt. All seven notebooks were downloaded (HTTP 200) and their JSON/source cells inspected without execution. The six experiment notebooks read main, rating-link, lay-rating and expert CSVs from a separate local osfstorage-archive tree, and also reference generated main.cleaned.csv files. what_we_could_compute: For S1-S6, recover analyzed participant counts by randomized arm/cell after reproducing the posted exclusion and rating-availability filters, and calculate per-participant lay/expert creativity, originality and appropriateness means, SDs and SEs by arm. Average S1's multiple idea scores within participant before computing between-person uncertainty. This addresses final.open_items on missing per-arm/per-cell counts and missing supplementary sub-dimension/expert summaries.

For S3 (Experiment 2B), calculate a comparison using only the two randomized human arms, excluding the 100 ChatbotOnly outputs from participant counts and the two-arm variance estimate; recalculate the AI-only score SD to resolve the printed 0.30 versus 0.40 discrepancy. The three-arm R code is available to audit the paper's pooled-model standardization. This addresses final.open_items on the pooled variance/d calculation and inconsistent AI-only SD.

For S3, join the expert notnew/incnew/radnew ratings to the idea links and observed conditions to calculate newness-type outcomes for each named arm, including separate ChatGPT-assisted, Human-only and AI-only results. This addresses the uncoded newness-type result and unresolved former S3-O3 contrast.

For S5 and S6, estimate the technology contrast pooled over the other randomized factor, alongside cell-specific means, SDs, SEs, counts and interactions, and inspect the posted models underlying the printed 'main effects'.

For S1, compute arm summaries and the test for idea_count_jc to investigate the inconsistent printed t/P pair. The posted code and participant scores also permit its top20percent analysis (OVERALL strictly above the pooled participant-score 80th percentile); an output-level share can be calculated separately from idea-level ratings and must not be silently equated with that participant-level code.

For S4, compute the available process-measure and articulateness summaries, including per-arm SDs/SEs, and reproduce mediation inputs; for S1-S4, expert articulateness/verbosity fields are available where recorded. These data permit many numerical checks referred to Supplementary Notes E-I even though the supplement itself was not retrieved.

For S4 (Experiment 3), recalculate the lay judges' mean age and female share from Exp3.rating.qualtrics.csv after applying the documented judge-selection filters, to check the reported demographic figures that duplicate the idea generators' figures. This can check the numbers, but cannot establish whether the publication error was a copy error.

For all six randomized studies, use nonempty idea texts linked to participant IDs and treatment conditions to compute within-arm semantic/text diversity and similarity, with participant-based aggregation or resampling for S1 and separate handling of S3's AI-only outputs. No ready-made embedding or diversity-score dataset was found; the measures must be calculated from the texts.
